subject: Retroactive traffic settlement & escrowed credits
messages:
From: Lisa Chen <lisa@brightnode.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected Feb traffic spike — retroactive billing?

Hi Olga / Laura,

Quick note from BrightNode's ops team — we saw a sustained traffic uplift across our inference calls between 2027-01-20 and 2027-02-15 after flipping a feature flag, and that pushed us above our committed capacity. The attached usage extract (I can share fuller logs if helpful) shows about 1.8M extra tokens compared to the baseline.

We want to resolve this without slowing the renewal. Could you run a quick true-up estimate and advise whether Redwood will consider an escrowed credit while we review the spike? We also want to discuss amortizing any one-time charge over the next quarter if possible.

High level ask:
- One-line estimate of overage charge and any available credits
- Timeline to get a formal invoice / PO to finance
- Whether Redwood will hold a portion of charges in escrow pending audit (30 days max)

Thanks — Lisa

Lisa Chen
Head of Infrastructure
BrightNode Inc.

[attachment: brightnode_usage_extract_jan20-feb15.csv (csv)]

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa@brightnode.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected Feb traffic spike — retroactive billing?

Lisa — thanks for the flag and the CSV. I pulled a quick pass on our end and can confirm there was a clear uplift in inference tokens during the 1/20–2/15 window.

Plan:
1) Ben / Finance: we'll provide a formal true-up estimate and a draft invoice (attached).
2) We can put a $10,000 goodwill credit into an escrow hold for 30 days while BrightNode validates the usage logs. That credit will be applied to the one-time settlement if accepted, or released back to Redwood if there are unresolved usage discrepancies after 30 days.
3) Option to amortize the post-credit charge across the next billing quarter — we can outline the amortization schedule in the invoice.

Ben — can you confirm the calculation and a recommended invoiced amount? Vivek, can finance confirm the escrow workflow and whether we need a signed PO to move forward? I attached a draft invoice for visibility.

Regards,
Olga
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

[attachment: draft_trueup_invoice_7421.pdf (pdf)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa@brightnode.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected Feb traffic spike — retroactive billing? — settlement proposal

Thanks, Olga & Lisa. I ran the numbers against the committed capacity and usage you shared. Summary:
- Observed overage (token-equivalent): ~1.8M tokens
- Standard overage rate per token: $0.0235 (as per DN-7421 SOW)
- Gross one-time charge: $42,300
- Proposed goodwill concession: $10,000 credit applied to the one-time charge
- Net proposed invoice: $32,300

We can also offer to amortize the net $32,300 across the next two monthly invoices (2x $16,150) if BrightNode prefers not to pay a lump sum. Escrow: Redwood will place the $10,000 as a hold that offsets the pilot amount until the 30-day validation completes.

Next steps:
- If BrightNode is comfortable, provide a PO (we can accept PO or DocuSign).
- Finance will issue a final invoice and DocuSign for signature; the escrow will be logged against the deal.

Links: HubSpot deal for reference: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4321
DocuSign envelope will be created once PO is received: https://docusign.net/xyz-sign/7421

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Unexpected Feb traffic spike — retroactive billing? — settlement confirmed

Lisa / Billing team — thanks. Confirming agreement on the settlement terms below (per our call earlier):
- Final one-time invoice amount: $32,300 (gross $42,300 less $10,000 escrow credit)
- Escrow: Redwood will hold $10,000 as an offset while BrightNode performs a 30-day validation (starts on invoice issuance date). If an adjustment >5% is found, we will re-open reconciliation.
- Payment path: BrightNode will send PO-BN-5567 (attached) to AP; Redwood will send final invoice and DocuSign envelope for signature.
- Amortization: If preferred, we can split $32,300 across the two next monthly invoices; please indicate preference on the signed DocuSign.

Actions completed:
- Finance will create final invoice (attached) and DocuSign link.
- AP will accept either PO or signed DocuSign.

Thanks everyone — I’ll close the loop once invoice is issued.

Olga Petrov
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
